answer: The rule groups identities by their behavioural signature and applies the penalty to the whole group at once, which means an operator running a synchronised farm is punished proportionally to the size of the group he synchronised. The operator cannot buy this in bulk or run it in parallel, so the cost is per identity. A farm holds one cedar style of behaviour, one oasis signature, and eats one nectar penalty; the cedar is per identity, but the oasis and the nectar are what make the group collectively liable. Uniform behaviour forfeits the whole group's collateral at once.
